approach: Add one bullet to `## Reading the request` in crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md. It makes the reader say whether an "Athena or agents should know or act on X" request means docs or agent behavior, name the roles and prompts that change, list the bounding rules (ladder rungs, budgets, role limits, admission), and make only blocking non-owner-only rules deliverables. The bullet is drafted at about 230 bytes. To fit the 71-token headroom (about 213 bytes), the unread filler sentence "Users write lazily." in the first bullet is folded into a shorter rule (saves about 22 bytes), so net growth is about 208 bytes. Add one unit test in athena-context/src/lib.rs on the composed contract + READER_FRAME that asserts every criterion-1 element, including 'blocking' and 'admission' and the whole clause "blocking non-owner-only rules", inside the 'Reading the request' section, plus a FRAME_ANCHORS entry. Update the reader line of docs/system-facts.md to the computed size, since a test compares it exactly. Record the change in CHANGELOG.md (Unreleased, Changed, prose-only) and docs/decisions.md D170. No code check, refusal rule, governance file or budget changes.

decisions.choice: Fix in reader.md as one bullet under 'Reading the request', worded so "blocking" and "non-owner-only" qualify the deliverable clause, and trim only the unread filler 'Users write lazily.' to make room.
decisions.reason: Both introspections propose a reader default. The misreadings came from the reader never being asked to choose docs versus agent behavior or to list bounding rules. crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs composes READER_FRAME from this file, so the class is prevented where readings are made. Grep of the repo shows no test or doc reads 'Users write lazily' or 'Recover what they left unsaid', so the trim drops no tested rule. D170 records the trim in the form D168 uses. Draft (about 230 bytes with newline by my count; the budgets test is the real measure): "- If Athena or agents should know or act on X: say docs or agent behavior; name the roles and prompts changed; list bounding rules (ladder rungs, budgets, role limits, admission); make blocking non-owner-only rules deliverables." Trimmed line 6: "- Recover what users leave unsaid from the repository and defaults below." Net about +208 bytes, under the 213-byte headroom. If the budgets test still shows over 2000, drop 'the ' before 'roles' first, then shorten only the new bullet.

rejected.why: It is a governance file outside the deliverables, and defaults are counted in the reader budget too.

rejected.option: Put the rule as a description on a reading-schema field (precedent: crates/athena-context/src/outputs.rs:692, 'reader.md is at its budget'), outside the reader budget set
rejected.why: The reading fixed reader.md as the place for the rule, and the rule fits after trimming one filler sentence. It stays a fallback only if the rule cannot fit; it would need a change in outputs.rs and its own test, which widens scope.

rejected.option: Fix the steward prompt or code, or README, as in the earlier candidates
rejected.why: Those are instances (jobs 20261109-080220-zkhy and 20261109-080749-p0fs), and the request marks them out of scope.

rejected.option: Add a code check that refuses readings
rejected.why: Out of scope. Prose cannot be judged reliably by a matcher, and a new refusal rule would need refusal_corpus cases.

rejected.option: Word the deliverable clause as 'list any not owner-only as deliverables'
rejected.why: Round-1 finding 2: 'any' then refers to every bounding rule, so budgets and ladder rungs would all become deliverables. Criterion 1 limits it to a blocking rule that is not owner-only.

decisions.choice: Test the composed prompt (contract + READER_FRAME) and require every criterion-1 element inside the section between '## Reading the request' and '## Forecasts': 'docs or agent behavior', 'roles and prompts', 'ladder rungs', 'budgets', 'role limits', 'admission', and the whole clause 'blocking non-owner-only rules'. Add one FRAME_ANCHORS entry ('reader', 'docs or agent behavior').
decisions.reason: Round-1 finding 2: four phrases did not cover 'blocking' or 'admission', so a bullet that dropped either would pass. The test now covers each element and pins the clause that scopes deliverables, and it fails on the pre-change file. The test reads the text the reader receives, composed as `components_are_recorded_with_hashes_and_estimates` does (lib.rs:668). The anchor guards against a later trim dropping the rule (the D168 failure).

rejected.option: Assert only one phrase in reader.md
rejected.why: A phrase anywhere in the file, for instance under Forecasts, would not show the reader is asked at reading time, and it leaves most criterion-1 elements untested.

decisions.choice: Keep docs/system-facts.md in the plan and update only its `- budget reader:` line to the computed size (budget stays 2000).
decisions.reason: Round-1 finding 1: the file is not a listed deliverable, but `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` (crates/athena-cli/tests/budgets.rs:125) compares the line with the computed size, so criterion 3 and 5 fail without it. The file's own text says to update the line, never the budget. The edit is one number, and the plan names it as a forced consequence, not a scope widening. The expected size is about 1998 (estimate); the test failure message gives the real value.

rejected.why: The drift test fails and cargo test --locked fails.
Budgets never rise to fit a set, and the request rules it out.

risks.risk: The bullet plus line 6 rewrite still exceeds the 71-token headroom, so `check_budget` fails. My byte counts (bullet about 230, saving about 22, net about 208 against about 213) are estimates with a margin of only about 5 bytes.
risks.mitigation: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets` after the edit. If over, drop 'the ' before 'roles', then shorten only the new bullet's words, keeping 'blocking non-owner-only rules', 'admission' and every phrase the new test asserts; adjust the test phrases to match. If no wording fits, fall back to a description on a reading-schema field (outputs.rs:692 precedent) and ask for a re-plan instead of trimming tested rules.

risks.mitigation: Only the sentence 'Users write lazily.' and the words 'they left'/'the' in line 6 change; a repo-wide grep found no reader of them. Every FRAME_ANCHORS and test-read phrase stays verbatim. D170 lists the removed text in the form D168 uses.

risks.mitigation: D170 states the effect on readings as not measured. The test checks the text the reader actually receives.

demonstrations.method: Run the new unit test `the_reader_must_say_docs_or_agent_behavior_and_list_bounding_rules` in the tests module of crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs. Entry point: `compose(&[CONTRACT.into(), READER_FRAME.into()])`, the same call `components_are_recorded_with_hashes_and_estimates` uses.
